claims.summary: Synchronous success is appropriate when the entire batch completes within the 30-second response window. Here 12 elapsed seconds plus another minute exceeds that boundary, so this is not the required in-window plan.

A successful durable queue acceptance takes the stated two seconds and precedes 202, leaving unfinished processing to the queue worker. Event Grid treats 202 as acknowledgement of the whole batch; the key depends on successful acceptance, not merely starting a send.

503 is an appropriate retryable response when the endpoint cannot accept the batch. All-or-none batching then requests replay of the batch, which is the alternative recovery path rather than the successful durable handoff required here.

sourceReviews.supportingSummary: Re-read the complete delivery unit: 200–204 acknowledge, 202 supports asynchronous acceptance, response wait is 30 seconds, 503 is a transient retry response, and output batches use all-or-none acknowledgement. Detailed endpoint-specific rules qualify its overbroad introductory retry sentence. No exact-once or immediate dead-letter write guarantee is adopted.

Re-read the full broker unit. The producer can hand work to a durable queue and a separate consumer processes at its own pace. This supports the configured worker handoff, not the unit’s broader no-loss/proportional-scaling or exactly-once-sounding allocation wording.

Re-read all receive, settlement, DLQ and long-work sections. Reliable processing retains explicit acknowledgement/failure boundaries and durable work must be recorded before early completion. The item does not promise exactly-once external effects or an atomic Event Grid/Service Bus transaction.

choiceReviews.rationale: Twelve seconds already elapsed and another minute of synchronous work would reach about 72 seconds, beyond the source’s 30-second endpoint response window. Correct-when context: Synchronous completion is appropriate when the whole batch can finish and acknowledge inside the response window. That timing condition is absent here.

The queue durably accepts the remaining job in the supplied two seconds before the response; 14 elapsed seconds fits the window. Event Grid accepts 202 for the whole batch and the supplied worker can process the accepted remaining work independently. Correct-when context: This design is valid only after confirmed durable queue acceptance, not merely after starting a send. A failed enqueue removes the premise for acknowledging success.

503 is retryable, and the unit’s all-or-none batching makes that response request replay of the entire batch instead of the required durable handoff without requesting batch replay. Correct-when context: Use 503 when the endpoint cannot accept the batch and a whole-batch retry is the desired recovery path.

Downloading remote settings is documented for reproducing configuration in local development. It does not rebuild or redeploy interpreter-specific artifacts and is not a replacement for the stated version-change obligation.
Registered blueprints organize and expose handlers across Python modules. They are useful for modular application structure but do not rebuild dependencies when the interpreter version changes.
